summary:
Terra Analogues is a web app that explains why scientists use certain places on Earth to prepare for the Moon and Mars, and where each comparison stops working.

The app has three steps. Explore Earth shows six analogue sites, including the La Corona lava tube in Lanzarote and the acidic Dallol springs in Ethiopia. Each site has a short story and NASA satellite images of the site beside its Moon or Mars counterpart. Dual Map places the Earth site next to its target using NASA GIBS, Moon Trek and Mars Trek layers. Compare scores the pair across seven dimensions (geology, terrain, temperature, ice, dust, caves and habitability), gives a plain-language verdict, and lists what Earth cannot reproduce: gravity, atmosphere and radiation.

The challenge asks teams to use open NASA data to show what makes a site analogous, how similar it is, and where the analogy breaks down. Terra Analogues answers those questions for every site it covers.

Missions like Artemis test equipment and crew procedures on Earth before launch. Choosing the right site for each test, and knowing its limits, lowers the risk of those missions.
details:
Terra Analogues is a website that shows which places on Earth are like the Moon or Mars. Scientists use these places to test equipment before space missions.

The site has three steps. First, you pick one of six places on a world map, such as a lava tube in Spain or a salt desert in Chile. Each place has a short story with NASA photos of the place and of its Moon or Mars match. Second, the Dual Map shows both places side by side. Third, the Compare page gives a similarity score and explains what is the same and what is different. It also shows what Earth can never copy, like low gravity and space radiation.

This helps mission teams choose the right place to test their equipment, and it helps students learn how space missions are prepared.

We built it with React, TypeScript and Python, using free NASA data from GIBS, Moon Trek and Mars Trek. It is stored on GitHub and runs on Netlify. We also used an AI coding assistant to help write the code.

What makes it different is that it shows the weak points of each match, not just the good ones. We kept it simple with only three steps, used real NASA images of each place, and made the pages load quickly.
